title: helm(private): stabilize encryption init hooks and nodeselector compatibility
author: Claire Huang
description: Stabilize Helm init hooks for the private deployment chart to address flakiness during upgrade/rollback paths and ensure init jobs respect nodeSelectors and KMS configuration. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in constrained on-prem clusters reported intermittent failures during upgrades where the encryption-init job either failed to schedule (missing nodeSelector/taints) or reran on rollback causing key duplication. This PR standardizes hook weights and ordering, surfaces validation errors for missing KMS config in values.schema.json v3, and splits the legacy init job into explicit pre-upgrade and post-rollback hooks. Includes tests that exercise upgrade and rollback flows against a lightweight kind cluster used in CI.
commits: Refactor: split encryption init job into hooks/upgrade-init-job.yaml (pre-upgrade) and hooks/rollback-cleanup-job.yaml (post-rollback)
Fix: thread nodeSelector, tolerations, and affinity through templates to ensure init jobs schedule on private nodes
Add: values.schema.json v3 validations for .private.encryption.kms.provider and required secret refs
Test: add tests/helm/upgrade-rollback.sh to reproduce upgrade -> rollback sequence; add helm-chart test harness job
Docs: document migration notes for values.encryption -> values.private.encryption and behaviour during rollback
review_conversation: Asha Patel: Can you add explicit nodeSelector/tolerations to the init hooks? We see scheduling in single-purpose nodes in several customer clusters.
Claire Huang: Added nodeSelector/tolerations/affinity passthrough in _helpers.tpl and wired into both hook templates; defaults to empty to preserve current behaviour.
Diego Martinez: The hook weights looked suspicious — pre-upgrade hook should run before CRD migrations. Can we set weight to -5 and add an explicit helm.sh/resource-policy where relevant?

Claire Huang: Set upgrade-init weight to -5 and rollback-cleanup to 50; added note in templates explaining ordering rationale and the reason for conservative weights to avoid race with migration hooks.
Rohit Singh: CI caught an edge case where the KMS secret name was optional — that can lead to silent failures. Please make the schema require provider and secret when encryption.enabled is true.
Claire Huang: Updated values.schema.json v3 to require .private.encryption.kms.provider and .private.encryption.kms.secretRef when .private.encryption.enabled == true.
Asha Patel: Approved after CI green and tests added that validate upgrade+rollback sequence in kind-based job.
Merge-bot: Merged via squash (squash merge) at 2025-02-21.

release_notes: Fix: Stabilize encryption init hooks for redwood-private Helm chart. Ensure init jobs respect nodeSelector/tolerations/affinity; add schema validation for KMS configuration when encryption is enabled; improve upgrade/rollback ordering to avoid key duplication on rollback. Chart version bumped to 1.12.3. No breaking behavioral changes for default installs, but clusters with custom encryption values should review migration notes.
notes_for_ops: Operators: when upgrading from versions <1.11.0 that used values.encryption, confirm your encryption values have been migrated to values.private.encryption per docs. If you rely on custom scheduling for init jobs, set private.nodeSelector and private.tolerations in values.yaml. The upgrade job now has weight -5 to run prior to common migration hooks; rollback cleanup runs at weight 50 to ensure it executes after resource deletions.
tests_added: tests/helm/upgrade-rollback.sh (bash harness that runs helm upgrade --install -> create dummy data -> helm rollback -> verify cleanup and idempotence)
changelog_entry: 1.12.3 - Fix: Stabilize encryption init hooks and add KMS validation for private deployments. See migration notes for encryption values.
additional_context: This PR was prompted by support case SUP-879 where a customer experienced duplicated encryption keys after an interrupted upgrade. The change is narrowly scoped to the redwood-private Helm chart and does not affect the hosted API or dedicated runtime. Follow-up PR planned to add a Helm test matrix for nodeSelector/toleration permutations across major cluster configs.
